title: Address Element / Registration Threat Model
surface: Embedded address entry, postal assist, AGID assist, correction feedback
reviewCadence: Every public widget release and every new host integration
privacyGoal: Let users enter or correct an address locally while public host events expose only quality state, country, language, and commitments.
nonGoals: Prove legal residence
Store a public address book
Train on private corrections without explicit opt-in

misuseCases.title: Host page exfiltrates raw draft through events
misuseCases.scenario: A merchant embeds the element and records each keystroke or correction as plain text.
primaryControls: host contract forbids raw draft callbacks

misuseCases.title: Feedback becomes a private address training feed
misuseCases.scenario: Correction feedback is synced and reused for learning without consent or redaction.

dataMinimizationRules: Keep draft text in component state until explicit submit.
Host events carry commitment, status, country, language, and issue category only.
highRiskModeRequirements: Prefer coarse AGID or AGID-S handoff.
openQuestions: Which host event names are stable public API?
Which feedback categories can be learned without private text?
requiredInvariants: No raw address, raw AOID, AGID-S payload, proof code, recipient secret, precise private coordinates, or witness material crosses public or shared boundaries by default.
AOID must not become a global public tracking identifier.
Purpose, audience, and retention must be explicit before any disclosure leaves local state.
High-risk mode prefers coarse disclosure, short-lived aliases, local proof checks, immediate revocation or used-state marking, and no address-history retention.

title: Address Portal Consent Threat Model
surface: User consent, scope, revoke, delete, export, and Address Item management
reviewCadence: Every new scope, issuer, export type, or deletion workflow
privacyGoal: Let a user see, revoke, delete, and export who may use address-derived facts without exposing the address itself.
nonGoals: Make revocation paid-only
Let a third party silently expand scopes
Use AOID as a public profile id
trustBoundaries: user consent screen to relying party

misuseCases.title: Scope confusion grants more than the user understood
misuseCases.scenario: A relying party requests delivery and identity scopes with misleading UI copy.
primaryControls: deny by default for unknown scopes

misuseCases.title: Export leaks private address material
misuseCases.scenario: A user export includes raw AOID body, private evidence, or proof secrets.

dataMinimizationRules: Portal lists relying parties and scopes, not raw address text.
Export defaults to commitments and references unless user explicitly requests local private backup.
highRiskModeRequirements: No history retention after high-risk handoff.
openQuestions: Which scopes are mandatory for each integration?
What export format is safe for nontechnical users?
requiredInvariants: No raw address, raw AOID, AGID-S payload, proof code, recipient secret, precise private coordinates, or witness material crosses public or shared boundaries by default.
AOID must not become a global public tracking identifier.
Purpose, audience, and retention must be explicit before any disclosure leaves local state.
High-risk mode prefers coarse disclosure, short-lived aliases, local proof checks, immediate revocation or used-state marking, and no address-history retention.

title: POS Terminal Handoff Threat Model

privacyGoal: Let staff decide whether to accept, reject, or complete a handoff without storing address bodies or reusable proof secrets.
nonGoals: Replace carrier compliance systems
Store customer address history in POS logs

misuseCases.title: Copied QR is reused after the handoff
misuseCases.scenario: An attacker screenshots a QR and replays it at a different counter.

misuseCases.title: Audit report stores the private delivery payload
misuseCases.scenario: The report stores QR body, address text, proof code, or recipient details.

dataMinimizationRules: Reports store terminal signature, alias, status, roots, and commitments only.
Printers receive formatted redacted receipt output.
highRiskModeRequirements: No precise address on printed receipt.
openQuestions: Which terminals need hardware key storage?
Which carriers accept recipient proof status without full address disclosure?

misuseCases.title: Offline queue is stolen from device storage

misuseCases.title: Reachability reports expose vulnerable locations

dataMinimizationRules: Conflict records carry aliases, nullifiers, vector clocks, and redacted reasons.

misuseCases.title: OCR draft leaks to server logs
misuseCases.scenario: A document parser or debug logger sends extracted address text to a server.

misuseCases.title: Verifier receives the source document unnecessarily

dataMinimizationRules: OCR text is editable local draft until user confirms.
Verifier receives commitment, status, or proof instead of the document by default.
highRiskModeRequirements: No persistent source document unless encrypted.
Short retention and local delete path.

Which evidence classes require legal hold controls?

title: ZK Address Predicate Threat Model

reviewCadence: Every proof relation, public signal schema, circuit, or verifier release
privacyGoal: Prove address-derived facts without revealing the address, AOID body, exact location, witness, or private credential material.
nonGoals: Claim production cryptographic assurance without audit
Use ZK to prove real-world truth without issuer/evidence model

misuseCases.title: Public signals leak a unique location
misuseCases.scenario: The public statement exposes a region, timestamp, or predicate so narrow that it identifies the holder.

misuseCases.title: Cross-proof nullifier links unrelated actions
misuseCases.scenario: The same nullifier domain is used for residence, delivery, and aid claims.

dataMinimizationRules: Witnesses never leave local proving context.
Public signals contain only predicate id, scope, roots, challenge, and domain-separated nullifier if needed.
highRiskModeRequirements: Avoid permanent public proof anchoring unless required.
openQuestions: Which predicates have enough anonymity sets?
Which proof systems are production-ready after audit?

title: AGID-S QR/NFC Sharing Threat Model

nonGoals: Put AGID-S ciphertext on public ledgers by default
Use permanent exact location QR for high-risk cases
trustBoundaries: decryptor to POS or field app

misuseCases.title: Copied AGID-S remains useful too long
misuseCases.scenario: A copied QR is scanned later by a different party after the intended handoff.

misuseCases.title: Parser logs decrypted AGID
misuseCases.scenario: The scanner debug log stores plaintext after decryption.

dataMinimizationRules: Payload contains AGID, expiry, purpose, and jti only when needed.
Public logs store ciphertext hash or alias, not plaintext or production ciphertext sample.

How are lost reader keys revoked?
